webpage.description: This is a very old and yet newish project. Back in the late 1980's I began to build a Z80 based computer. The Interak, produced by Greenbank electronics in Liverpool, the attraction for me was you could build it bit by bit, board by board,  It fitted in a 3U high 19" rack, you could jump on it without harming it, built like a tank.. I had many years of fun and learning my basic electronics with it. But then I sold it a few years later and got my first PC. About 2 years ago now someone discovered it in a rubbish skip in cambridge (along with a CPM book with my details inside), I had sold it to a company out there. and i was able own it once again..... so I've turned full circle, with a lot of other stuff between.. Pics and Arduinos tec..
webpage.title: Interak Z80 Computer

webpage.description:
In my quest to get the last x86 version of BeOS running, I've had to spend a long time testing out different emulators to see what works. Adafruit has recently written a post about getting it to work on VirtualBox [https://learn.adafruit.com/build-a-bebox-with-beos-and-virtualbox?view=all], though I suspect because I have an AMD computer, I can't get it to do anything but guru-medidate on me, so I had to come up with my own solution.

To follow in my steps, here's what you'll need:

 * A copy of BeOS Professional 5.0 for Intel x86 [https://winworldpc.com/product/beos/5]
   * You'll need to create a .cue file for the image, as described in the Adafruit article [https://learn.adafruit.com/build-a-bebox-with-beos-and-virtualbox/set-up-the-cd-image]
 * PCem [https://pcem-emulator.co.uk/]
 * BIOS files for the supported machines [https://github.com/BaRRaKudaRain/PCem-ROMs]
 * A PCap setup if you want to use networking (and SLiRP doesn't work)
   * Npcap [https://nmap.org/npcap/windows-10.html] and Win10Pcap [http…
